title: Cross-variant deterministic pinning and performance-profile export for embedding + reranker bundles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We currently have intermittent nondeterminism when generating pinned artifact bundles for dual-stage embedding+reranker candidates. This causes small but measurable variance in the published performance profiles (latency and token cost) between repeated pin exports for the same model+config. That variance blocks reliable canary rollouts and customer audits.

Goal: Implement a deterministic export pipeline for pinned model bundles (encoder + reranker pair) that: (1) ensures byte-stable manifests and artifact checksums given the same model versions and build inputs; (2) captures a canonical performance profile (latency P50/P95, memory footprint, throughput at target batch sizes and sequence lengths) computed under a reproducible harness; and (3) publishes both the pinned bundle and the profile to the model catalog with metadata for automated admission gates and rollouts.

Scope: encoder+reranker pairs (biencoder + cross-encoder reranker variants) for embeddings + reranking onboarding. Includes export tooling changes, CI harness updates, and catalog publish flow.

Out of scope: full cross-architecture quantization testing, dedicated capacity autoscaling changes, UI work in Console (will add follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Repeated pin-export runs for the same input (model versions, tokenizer checksum, export config) produce identical manifest.json and artifact checksums
Automated performance profile runs (CI harness) record stable P50/P95 latency within ±3% across three runs for the canonical inputs
Published pinned bundle in model catalog includes: model pins, build-id, runtime-compatibility matrix, and the performance-profile artifact with raw measurements and summary metrics
Admission gate can reference the profile to automatically allow/deny canary rollouts based on configured latency and quality thresholds
End-to-end smoke: import pinned bundle to a staging Dedicated cluster and run a simple canary traffic job using the published profile; job completes without schema or compatibility errors
tasks: Design deterministic packaging format and manifest fields (include build inputs, tokenizer checksum, dependency locks)
Make export pipeline order-deterministic (file ordering, stable tar creation, canonical JSON ordering)
Add content-addressable checksums and attestations for artifacts
Extend CI performance harness to run three repeatable trials with controlled seeds and pinned hardware config
Record and store raw latency traces and summarized metrics in profile artifact
Integrate profile publishing step with catalog service and ensure backward-compatible schema
Create admission gate hook to reference profile thresholds for canary decisions
Add unit/integration tests and a short smoke playbook for SRE to validate staging imports
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial intake. Noted a few customer-facing incidents where repeated pin exports changed checksums and customers could not reproduce results. Adding deterministic packaging as a priority to unblock audits.

2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Spike completed — nondeterminism primarily caused by unordered file inclusion and metadata timestamps in the archive. Proposal: canonical JSON dumps + zeroed timestamps + lexicographic ordering before tar creation.

2026-03-05 - Marta Silva (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; asked that the profile includes both microbenchmarks (single-request latency) and batch throughput curves for 1, 8, 16 batch sizes. Also requested a field for 'test_harness_version' in the published profile.

2026-03-07 - Liam Chen: Implemented stable-archive prototype in feature branch: github.com/redwood/infra/PR-1389. Early tests show identical manifests for local repeats. Need to run CI harness on pinned GPU runner to validate performance stability.

2026-03-09 - Security Review (note): team to confirm no secret material ends up in manifest; using content-addressable checksum only. Marking security_review_required=true and adding follow-up to security checklist.

2026-03-10 - QA: Ran three harness trials on staging-nvidia-a100-40GB; P50 variance 1.8%, P95 variance 2.6% across runs for the sample model. Raw traces uploaded to internal perf dashboard. Next: integrate publish step to catalog and run full smoke import.
